items.note: The page states the identity $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}{T}$ under the paper's hypothesis 'When every $t_i$ is even' and proves it as the paper does: periodicity of $a$, the coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$ on the right, and a match with the coefficient of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ computed from $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ and the normalized negative-sign transform.

This is a definition, and the page gives it exactly as the paper does: '$a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$, a phase quadratic in the index', with $\overline a$ its conjugate. Since nothing can be derived for a definition, I count it as fully present.

The page works out the change in the exponent, '$-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$', and says it is an integral multiple of $2\pi i$ 'because $t_i$ is even' ($s_i$ is an integer). It also gives the reason periodicity matters: the convolution reads $a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}$ modulo $t_i$.

The page expands with '$(j_i-k_i)^2=j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2$' and writes the combined exponent as $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2)$. The signs are right and this reduces to $2\pi i s_ij_ik_i/t_i$, matching the paper's displayed coefficient.

In its Setting section the page defines $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ with $\frac1T$ and $\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, and $Q$ as 'position $\boldsymbol j$ holds the entry of frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$'. Substituting $f_i=-s_ij_i$ gives the coefficient $\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_i s_ij_ik_i/t_i)$, which the page matches, as the paper does.

errors.quote: The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.
errors.problem: The convolution is $d$-dimensional, on $\prod_i\mathbb Z/t_i\mathbb Z$ with $T$ entries. The paper calls it 'cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups', and the page itself takes indices modulo each $t_i$. It is not a one-dimensional cyclic convolution of length $T$, and since the $t_i$ are powers of two the two groups are not isomorphic when $d>1$.
